messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] duma
parts:
On 11/30/12 5:47 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> I tried to run test-unit linking to the duma library
>
> http://duma.sourceforge.net/

Thanks for running this. I'm a big fan of automatic
fault detection.

> which is intended "to detect buffer overruns and under-runs in C and C++ programs". It alleges there are 37 such
> problems in Stan:
>
> |
> Segmentation fault
> make: *** [runtest/test/io/reader] Error 139
> DUMA 2.5.15 (shared library, NO_LEAKDETECTION)

>
> There is a detailed explanation as to what to do at
>
> http://duma.sourceforge.net/README.txt

Their README says this:

-------------------
DUMA uses the virtual memory hardware of your computer to place an inaccessible
memory page immediately after (or before, at the user's option) each memory
allocation. When software reads or writes this inaccessible page, the hardware
issues a segmentation fault, stopping the program at the offending instruction.
It is then trivial to find the erroneous statement using your favorite
debugger. In a similar manner, memory that has been released by free() is made
inaccessible, and any code that touches it will get a segmentation fault.
--------------------

I don't think this strategy is sound for our arena-based
memory usage, which allocates contiguous subblocks within
a larger block of memory. I'm less skeptical about the
locations that don't touch that memory. I rarely use
stepwise debuggers myself because I find them incredibly hard
to follow compared to instrumenting with print statements.
But this is a good excuse to try it out and see where it
thinks the seg fault's coming from.

Partly I'm thinking that if we had segfault issues all over
like this, that they'd actually be tickled by our tests
or our regular usage, and as far as I know, we've never seen
this happen.
> It might be nice if Jenkins linked to duma by default.

I'm all for adding it to Jenkins once I'm convinced it's
not going to just give us a long list of false positives.
If it's slow, I'm sure Daniel could configure it like the
model tests to run daily rather than on every commit.

- Bob
